title: CANDI: Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Diffusion Models
claim: Existing approaches each capture only one of two desirable properties; our hybrid approach combines both in a single process.
layout: 3 stacked rows, left-to-right denoising flow, ✓/✗ property badges per row
description: Three horizontal rounded bands compare Masked Diffusion (pink/red, top), Continuous Diffusion (purple, middle) and Hybrid Diffusion (green, bottom, labeled CANDI). Each row has a title at left, with two badges that show a green check or red cross for 'Uses Discrete Conditioning' and 'Uses Joint Updates'. The masked row has a check for discrete conditioning and a cross for joint updates. The continuous row has the reverse. The hybrid row has two checks. To the right, a left-to-right flow of token grids passes through denoiser blocks. Masked diffusion starts with empty dashed boxes and fills in words like 'Discrete', 'is', 'diffusion', 'cool'. Continuous and hybrid rows start from a 3x4 grid of faint words and sharpen to a few solid tokens. The hybrid row uses a green lollipop CANDI mascot as the denoiser. The eye goes first to the colored row titles and check/cross badges.
caption: We provide a visual comparison of discrete, continuous, and hybrid diffusion. Discrete diffusion leverages discrete conditional structure, but lacks the ability to perform joint updates due to sampling each position independently. Continuous diffusion performs joint updates, but lacks discrete conditional structure. Our proposed hybrid diffusion, CANDI, can leverage both discrete conditional structure and joint updates.
abstract: While continuous diffusion has shown remarkable success in continuous domains such as image generation, its direct application to discrete data has underperformed pure discrete formulations. To understand this gap, we introduce token identifiability, an analytical framework characterizing how Gaussian noise corrupts discrete data through two mechanisms: discrete identity corruption and continuous rank degradation. We reveal that these mechanisms scale differently with vocabulary size, creating a temporal dissonance that forces a tradeoff between learning continuous geometry and discrete structure. To address this, we propose CANDI (Continuous ANd DIscrete diffusion), a hybrid framework that decouples discrete and continuous corruption, enabling simultaneous learning of both. This unlocks the benefits of continuous diffusion for discrete spaces: on controlled generation, CANDI enables classifier-based guidance with off-the-shelf classifiers through simple gradient addition; on text generation, CANDI outperforms masked diffusion at low NFE, demonstrating the value of learning continuous gradients for discrete spaces. We include the code on the project page: https://patrickpynadath1.github.io/candi-lander.
